app.desktopTitle: Open Bucky in the desktop app
app.desktopDesc: This page talks to the local Bucky core, which only runs inside the desktop app. Start it with task dev or the packaged app.

tray.attentionSub: Failed or paused; retry or resume

welcome.title: A little space for everything
welcome.desc: Connect your object storage account to browse, preview, share and move objects. Credentials stay in the system keychain or environment variables you choose.
welcome.pick: Pick a bucket in the sidebar to start browsing.

browser.readOnlyBanner: Read-only connection · Browse, preview, download and share are allowed. Upload, copy, move, delete and overwrite are disabled.
browser.readOnlyTip: Not allowed on a read-only connection

search.hint: Type a name to search this folder and its subfolders, or jump to any connection, bucket or folder.
search.noJump: No matching connections, buckets or folders

states.credDesc: Cloudflare R2 rejected the saved credentials, or they can’t be read. Edit the connection to update them.
states.netDesc: The network request failed. Check your network or proxy, then retry.
states.permDesc: These credentials can’t list objects in this bucket.
states.emptyBucketTitle: This bucket has no objects yet
states.emptyBucketDesc: Drop files or folders here, or click Upload.
states.emptyFolderDesc: Drop files to upload them to {{place}}.
states.readOnlyEmpty: Uploads are disabled on read-only connections.
states.noResultsDesc: Scanned {{count}} objects in {{place}} and its subfolders. Other folders aren’t searched.
states.loadingDesc: Large folders load page by page without blocking the window.

quicklook.failedDesc: The object couldn’t be loaded. Retry, or download it instead.
quicklook.expiredDesc: The presigned link passed its 1-hour lifetime and has to be created again.
quicklook.headersDesc: Reading this object requires request headers that the preview can’t attach. Download it instead.
quicklook.unsupportedDesc: Download it and open it in another app.
quicklook.truncated: File is {{size}}; showing the first 1 MiB
quicklook.note: Previews load through a presigned link that is valid for 1 hour and kept in memory only.

share.noPublic: This connection has no public access URL, so public links aren’t available.
share.publicWarn: Public links never expire. Anyone with the link can open it.
share.headers: Recipients must send these headers or the request is rejected:
share.folder: Folder share: {{count}} objects, one link each
share.more: {{count}} more links are included in Copy all
share.footTemporary: Temporary links are signed on this computer; Bucky doesn’t store them.
share.footPublic: Built from the connection’s public access URL.

plan.expired: This plan has expired and can’t run.
plan.warnDelete: Bucky can’t restore deleted objects. Once deleted, they can’t be recovered through Bucky.
plan.warnMove: Move copies to the destination, then deletes the source. Bucky can’t restore the source afterwards.
plan.warnOverwrite: {{count}} existing objects will be overwritten; the old content can’t be restored through Bucky.
plan.warnFolders: Includes folders; the plan lists every object under them.
plan.idNote: A plan ID isn’t consent. Sources and local files are checked again before running; if anything changed, nothing runs and you can create a new plan.
plan.confirm: I’ve reviewed this plan and want to run it
plan.verifying: Checking sources and local files again…
plan.changed: Objects changed after the plan was created, so nothing was run. Create the plan again to review the current state.
plan.interrupted: This plan was interrupted and won’t be resumed automatically.
plan.pickInvalid: A folder can’t be moved or copied into itself.
plan.pickSame: Choose a destination folder other than the current one.
plan.tooMany: A plan can contain up to 1,000 objects. Use the CLI for larger operations.

connection.r2Note: This version connects to Cloudflare R2 through its S3 API.
connection.name: Connection name
connection.keychainHint: Secrets are stored in the system keychain and never shown in plain text.
connection.environmentHint: Bucky reads these variables from its own process environment and never stores their values.
connection.accountIdError: The account ID has 32 hexadecimal characters
connection.keysBoth: Enter both the access key ID and the secret
connection.bucketHint: Leave empty to discover every bucket this account can access
connection.publicUrlHint: Used for public links and quick upload; must be HTTPS
connection.publicUrlError: Use an https:// URL without a query, fragment or credentials
connection.readOnlyHint: Allows browse, preview, download and share. Blocks upload, copy, move, delete and overwrite.
connection.deleteDesc: Only the local connection and its keychain credentials are removed. No objects in the cloud are deleted.
connection.deleted: Connection deleted; no cloud objects were affected

cloudflare.signInDesc: Bucky opens Cloudflare in your browser. After you authorize it, it creates an R2 token limited to the bucket you choose, so no key is ever typed or shown.
cloudflare.waitingHint: Finish the authorization in your browser. This window continues on its own once Cloudflare redirects back.
cloudflare.bucketHint: The R2 token is limited to this bucket
cloudflare.noBuckets: This account has no R2 buckets.
cloudflare.readOnlyHint: Creates a read-only R2 token: browse, preview, download and share.
cloudflare.scopeChangeHint: Saving a permission or jurisdiction change replaces the R2 token after verification.
cloudflare.accountMismatch: Sign in with the Cloudflare account used by this connection. The connection has not changed.
cloudflare.docs: How to create the OAuth client
cloudflare.tokenHint: Bucky verifies the new R2 token against this bucket before saving the connection.
cloudflare.authorizedNote: R2 token “{{token}}” · reauthorize to replace it
cloudflare.notAuthorizedNote: Authorize again to reconnect this bucket
cloudflare.disconnectDesc: The R2 token Bucky created is deleted on Cloudflare and the local credentials are removed. The connection stays, and no objects are touched.
cloudflare.prereq: Enable Account API Tokens Write when you authorize.
cloudflare.readyLead: Authorized as {{account}}. The R2 token Bucky creates reaches this bucket and nothing else.
cloudflare.featureBrowseDesc: Grid and list views with folders, previews and instant search across the bucket.
cloudflare.featureUsageDesc: A live breakdown by file type and size, scanned on demand.
cloudflare.featureShareDesc: Expiring pre-signed links, or your own public domain.
cloudflare.keychainNote: The credentials stay in the system keychain. Nothing is written to a config file.
cloudflare.stepMint: Bucky mints an R2 token limited to one bucket
cloudflare.stepVerify: Bucky verifies the token, then saves the connection
cloudflare.waitingAside: Bucky listens on a loopback address on this machine. Nothing is stored until the token has been verified against the bucket.
cloudflare.errorLead: Nothing was saved. Try again, or fall back to an access key.
cloudflare.setupRequired: No OAuth client ID is saved yet. Add one in settings, then start the sign-in again.
cloudflare.errorReason1: No OAuth client ID has been saved in settings.
cloudflare.errorReason2: Account API Tokens Write was not granted during authorization.
cloudflare.editLead: The account and bucket are fixed. Renaming the connection or changing the public URL keeps the current R2 token.

flow.title: Add connection
flow.desc: Connect a Cloudflare R2 bucket to Bucky

manual.title: Add with access keys
manual.lead: Create an R2 API token for the bucket in the Cloudflare dashboard, then paste its Access Key ID and Secret Access Key here.
manual.asideStep1: Open R2 → Manage API Tokens in the Cloudflare dashboard.
manual.asideStep2: Create a token with Object Read & Write, scoped to the bucket you want.
manual.asideStep3: Copy its Access Key ID and Secret Access Key into the form.
manual.asideNote: Both keys go to the system keychain. Only the Account ID and bucket name are written to the local database.

transfers.title: Transfers
transfers.cancelConfirm: Cancel this transfer? Temporary data is cleaned up; local files stay.

usage.title: Usage
usage.note: Scans list objects page by page in the background, don’t block browsing, and can be canceled anytime.
usage.idleDesc: A scan totals object count, size and the split by type and extension.
usage.partial: Scan canceled; results cover only what was scanned.
usage.noBucket: Open a bucket first to scan its usage.

settings.title: Settings
settings.usageHint: Scan the current bucket or prefix in the background.
settings.accentDesc: Used for selection, buttons and folder icons.
settings.rateLimitHint: Caps all transfers together. Applies to this desktop session.
settings.concurrencyHint: How many uploads and downloads run at the same time.
settings.mcpDesc: Add this snippet to your MCP client config. MCP exposes read and plan-creation tools only; uploads, downloads, deletes, copies, moves and plan execution go back to Bucky or the CLI for your confirmation.
settings.cliDesc: The bucky CLI shares the same local core and rules as the desktop app.
settings.skillDesc: The Agent Skill guides agents to read objects and create plans via the CLI or MCP; you still confirm every write in Bucky or the CLI.
settings.cloudflareDesc: Connections added with “Sign in with Cloudflare” need an OAuth client from your own Cloudflare account. Create it once and paste its client ID here.
settings.cloudflareSetup: In the Cloudflare dashboard open Manage Account → OAuth clients → Create client: name it Bucky, response type code, grant authorization_code, token auth method none, PKCE S256, then paste the redirect URL below into its Redirect URLs (press Enter to commit it) and tick Account Settings Read, Workers R2 Storage Read, Workers R2 Storage Bucket Item Write and the sensitive permission Account API Tokens Write.
settings.cloudflareClientIdHint: Kept locally with the other settings; never sent anywhere but Cloudflare.
settings.cloudflareRedirectHint: Must match the OAuth client exactly, loopback address included.
settings.cloudflareScopesHint: These scopes are requested when you sign in.
settings.tagline: A careful desktop client for object storage.
settings.privacyDesc: Credentials live only in the system keychain or environment variables you choose. They’re never shown, never logged, and no telemetry is sent.
settings.safetyDesc: Deletes, moves and overwrites always run from a plan you review and confirm. Read-only connections can’t change anything.

quick.tooLarge: Images up to 64 MiB can be uploaded here.
